title: George W. Erving to James Madison, Madrid, 24 Mar 1807, private No. 21 'in the Cypher of the Legation' (Pinckney's code), Founders Madison/02-13-02-0559

steps.what: Fetched RC1 (NARA M31 reel 12 frames 0283-0286) and RC2 (LoC tile URLs for mjm014714).
Transcribed the groups with Madison's interlinear readings into erving_groups.txt and collated the holes on both copies.
Read pairs from Pinckney's decoded despatches in the same code (reel 7 frames 0346-0352, reel 8 0083-0084): 69 in, 1515 late, 1578 that, 1583 ter.
Closed the printed holes: in the scale, Hanover (x5), see that he was more so, Gibraltar, been lately doing; Madison's slips identified.
Checked sp[eak] (1212 = sp): the rest of the word is missing in both copies, so the loss is Erving's own.

Page split under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): Erving's 24 Mar 1807 letter, in Pinckney's legation code (the = 1651), had shared the page legation.html with Adams's No. 88 in a different code (the = 1385); it now has its own page erving1807.html, card, badge and credits line. A reveal passage was built with the Pinckney key rebuilt in erving1807aug (build_reveal.py): 85 of the 97 groups of the Hanover runs have a value there.

outcome.method_basis: Madison's contemporary interlinear decode on RC1 (NARA M31 reel 12), printed in PJM-SS 13:529-31, gave the text; the printed holes were closed with code pairs from Pinckney's decoded despatches in the same code (reel 7 frames 0346-0352, reel 8 0083-0084).
outcome.fraction_read_source: NOTES Results: every hole in Madison's printed decode closed; no token-level reading file
outcome.notes: Read at the time by Madison; this project closed the holes in the printed text (a small completion). The only loss is Erving's dropped -eak after 1212, missing in both copies. No full Pinckney key was rebuilt (key: partial). Model id from commit trailers (Claude Opus 5, 1M context); the files were committed inside commits about other targets.

credits.note: Madison's interlinear decode (printed PJM-SS 13:529-31) and Pinckney's decoded despatches
